alerts.reason: Net sales went from 0.64% growth in December to a 3.87% decline in March. Higher prices partly offset a decline in pounds sold (A, B). I expect pricing to keep the June decline under 5%, with further volume losses widening the July–September decline to at least 5%.

The consolidated sales decline widened from 1.98% in December to 3.08% in March. Another 1.10 percentage points of deterioration per quarter would put June near -4.2% and July–September near -5.3%. Lower volumes and growing customer resistance to price increases support that trajectory (B, D).

Reported revenue growth slowed from 1.32% in December to -0.94% in March. Extending that 2.25-point deterioration gives about -3.2% in June and -5.4% in July–September. Revenue recognized from opening contract liabilities also fell about 30% year over year in March (A, B).

March revenue grew just 0.14%. A $0.3 billion IET gain offset a roughly equal OFSE decline across North America and international markets (A–C). I expect IET growth to keep June above -5%, with the oil-price pressure identified in D further weakening equipment and service demand by July–September.

The revenue decline widened from 1.49% in December to 2.41% in March as demand weakened for short-cycle equipment, parts and services (A, B). Backlog shipments can cushion June, but bookings covered only 80% of the $549 million shipped from backlog (C). That leaves less backlog to offset weak demand in July–September, when I expect the decline to reach 5%.

March total net revenue fell 3.11%, or $185.3 million, even as subscription and services revenue rose $208.7 million (A, B). Higher bitcoin prices partly offset fewer bitcoin sold (D). I expect those offsets to keep June above -5%, with continued bitcoin volume weakness putting July–September at risk of a decline of at least 5%.

Total revenue growth slowed from 7.36% in December to 3.24% in March, when revenue was $262.8 million (A). Repeating the unrounded 4.13-percentage-point slowdown gives roughly -0.9% in June and -5.02% in July–September. This trend-based forecast only narrowly crosses the threshold.

Total revenue fell 3.37% in March. Dedicated freight revenue rose $9.5 million, partly offsetting $13.9 million of combined declines in Expedited, Managed Freight and Warehousing, plus a $4.9 million fuel-surcharge decline (A, B). I expect Dedicated growth to keep June above -5%, with losses across the other businesses widening the decline to at least 5% in July–September.

Revenue growth fell from 1.54% in December to -0.74% in March. Continuing that pace implies about -3.0% in June and -5.3% in July–September. UPS had already begun reconfiguring its network in anticipation of lower volumes from its largest customer (E).
